title: A PCP-Level History: Thinking Traps, OPQRST and the Functional Enquiry

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already ask what happened, ask about pain, and check allergies and medications. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Turn a complaint into a short list of dangerous possibilities, and avoid thinking traps
  2. Take a deeper, organised history, including the functional enquiry (PCP only)
  3. Use the history to decide on protocols and PCP drugs

Textbook: Chapter 15, PDF pages 1303–1353
slides.say: Welcome. As EMRs, you already take histories every day: you ask what happened, ask about the pain, and check allergies and medications. So what changes now? As a PCP, the history does more work. It decides which protocol you follow, which drug you give, and which drug you must not give. BC also expects a deeper, more organised history from you, including a part that EMRs don't do at all. Today we'll cover three things: how to turn a chief complaint into a short list of dangerous possibilities without falling into thinking traps, how to build an organised history with the PCP functional enquiry, and how your history drives your PCP decisions.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎。作为 EMR，你们每天都在采集病史：问发生了什么、问疼痛、查过敏和用药。那现在有什么不同？作为 PCP，病史要承担更多：它决定你走哪个流程、给哪种药、哪种药绝对不能给。BC 还要求你采集更深入、更有条理的病史，其中有一部分 EMR 根本不做。今天讲三件事：怎样把主诉展开成一份危险可能的短清单，又不掉进思维陷阱；怎样按条理采集病史，包括 PCP 的系统问诊；以及病史怎样驱动你作为 PCP 的决定。

slides.title: Why the history matters more now
slides.body:
Before hospital, the history is most of your diagnosis

  • No lab tests or X-rays on scene: the story carries the weight
  • No working diagnosis → no protocol, no drug
  • Sick or not sick? Then: how sick?
  • Life threats first; then history and exam in any useful order
slides.say: In hospital, lab tests and X-rays often just confirm what the history already suggested. On scene, you don't have those tools, so the patient's story carries most of the weight. And as a PCP, you can't choose a protocol, or a drug, without a working diagnosis. Start every call by asking yourself: is this patient sick or not sick? Look at the chief complaint, the breathing, the pulse, the mental status and the skin. Then ask how sick. That tells you whether to treat on scene or in the ambulance. The initial assessment for life threats always comes first. After that, you can take the history and do the exam in whatever order serves the patient best.
slides.sayZh: 在医院，化验和影像常常只是证实病史已经提示的东西。现场没有这些工具，病人的叙述就承担了大部分分量。作为 PCP，没有工作诊断，你就选不了流程，也给不了药。每次出诊先问自己：这个病人病不病？看主诉、呼吸、脉搏、神志和皮肤。再问：有多重？这决定你在现场处理还是上车处理。找生命威胁的初始评估永远先做；之后，病史和查体的先后可以按对病人最有利的顺序安排。

slides.title: From complaint to a short list
slides.body:
Chief complaint→4–5 possibilities→rule out the worst first
  • Example, "weakness": low sugar, stroke, heart attack, infection, bleeding
  • Include the can't-miss causes, typical or not
  • Same system for the patient who calls every week
  • Jumping to a conclusion → wrong diagnosis → wrong treatment
slides.say: A chief complaint like weakness doesn't come with a label; the book calls it undifferentiated. Your job is to turn it into a short list of possible causes, called a differential diagnosis. Four or five is usually enough, as long as the list includes the dangerous, can't-miss ones. For weakness, you might think of low blood sugar, stroke, a heart attack, an infection, or hidden bleeding. Then you use your questions and your exam to rule the worst ones in or out first. Do this every time, even for the patient who calls nine-one-one every week. Jumping to a conclusion too early is a common reason for a wrong diagnosis, and then a wrong treatment.
slides.sayZh: 像「乏力」这样的主诉不会自带标签，书里叫它「未分化」主诉。你的任务是把它展开成一份可能原因的短清单，叫鉴别诊断。通常四到五个就够，只要包括危险、不能漏的那些。比如乏力，可以想到低血糖、卒中、心梗、感染或隐性出血。然后用问诊和查体，先把最危险的确认或排除。每次都这样做，哪怕是每周都打九一一的病人。过早下结论是误诊的常见原因，接着就是错误的治疗。

slides.title: Four thinking traps
slides.body:
TrapWhat it looks like
Premature closurestopping before other causes are ruled out
Anchoringone early detail locks your thinking
Confirmation biascollecting only the facts that agree
Ascertainment biasseeing what you expect: "it's flu season"

Your best defence: a systematic history, the same way every time.
slides.say: The book names four thinking traps, called cognitive biases. Premature closure is stopping too early: you accept a diagnosis before the other important ones are ruled out. Anchoring is when one early detail locks your thinking, like the word anxiety in the dispatch notes. Confirmation bias is collecting only the facts that agree with you, and ignoring the ones that don't. Ascertainment bias is seeing what you expect to see: in flu season, every cough becomes the flu. These traps matter more now, because as a PCP your diagnosis leads to drugs and fluids, not just oxygen and transport. The best defence is a systematic history, done the same way every time.
slides.sayZh: 书里点名了四种思维陷阱，叫认知偏差。过早闭合是太早收工：别的重要诊断还没排除，就接受了一个诊断。锚定是一条早期信息锁住了你的思路，比如派单备注里的「焦虑」两个字。确认偏差是只收集支持你的事实，忽视不支持的。查明偏差是只看到自己预期的东西：流感季节，每个咳嗽都成了流感。这些陷阱现在更要紧，因为作为 PCP，你的诊断会引出药物和补液，而不只是给氧和转运。最好的防线是系统化的病史，每次都按同样的方法做。

slides.q: A man who calls 9-1-1 most weeks says he has chest pain again. Your partner says, "It's just his anxiety." What is the best approach?
options: Agree, reassure him, and skip the full history to save time
Run your usual systematic history and rule out the dangerous causes first
Ask him to call his family doctor instead
Give oxygen and transport without questions, since he's a known patient
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A man who calls nine-one-one most weeks says he has chest pain again. Your partner says it's just his anxiety. What's the best approach? A, agree, reassure him, and skip the full history to save time. B, run your usual systematic history and rule out the dangerous causes first. C, ask him to call his family doctor instead. D, give oxygen and transport without questions, since he's a known patient. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。一位几乎每周都打九一一的男士说他又胸痛了。搭档说：「他就是焦虑。」最好的做法是什么？A 同意，安慰他，为省时间跳过完整病史；B 照常做系统化病史，先排除危险原因；C 让他改去找家庭医生；D 他是老病人，不问了，给氧直接送。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Calling it anxiety before you assess is anchoring and premature closure. Frequent callers get sick too, so use the same system and rule out the worst causes first. A skips the very step that protects him. C turns away care he may need. D treats without the history you need to choose the right protocol and to check drug contraindications.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。评估之前就认定是焦虑，属于锚定和过早闭合。常叫车的人也会真的生病，所以要用同样的方法，先排除最坏的原因。A 跳过了恰恰能保护他的那一步；C 拒绝了他可能需要的救治；D 没有病史就处置，你既选不准流程，也查不了药物禁忌。

slides.title: Building the history
slides.body:
Name + chief complaint→present illness→past history→current health
  • First responders there? Ask what they found and did
  • Open-ended first; build a timeline: what, then when
  • Injuries in about the last month; surgery or admissions in about 6 months
  • Prescription, over-the-counter and herbal drugs; allergies
  • Odd behaviour? Rule out hypoxia and low sugar first
slides.say: Here's the order the book suggests. On most calls, the two most important facts are the patient's name and the chief complaint. If first responders are there, ask what they found and what they've done, so the patient doesn't repeat everything. Start the present illness with an open-ended question, like tell me what happened, and build a timeline: what happened, and when. Then the past history, including injuries in about the last month and operations or hospital stays in about the last six months. Then current health: prescription, over-the-counter and herbal drugs, and allergies. And if the behaviour seems strange, rule out physical causes like low oxygen or low blood sugar before you think of a psychiatric cause.
slides.sayZh: 书里建议的顺序是这样。多数出诊最重要的两条是病人的姓名和主诉。如果第一响应者在场，先问他们发现了什么、做了什么，免得病人什么都重说一遍。现病史用开放式问题开头，比如「说说发生了什么」，再理出时间线：发生了什么、什么时候。然后是既往史，包括大约一个月内的受伤和大约六个月内的手术或住院。再是当前健康状况：处方药、非处方药、草药，以及过敏。如果行为看起来异常，先排除缺氧、低血糖这类生理原因，再考虑精神科原因。

slides.title: Getting the real story
slides.body:
TechniqueWhat it sounds like
Reflection"Can't breathe?" (their own words back)
Clarification"What do you mean by 'my sugars'?"
Empathy"That sounds really frightening."
Confrontationcalmly name what doesn't fit
Interpretation"If I understand you right…"

Lay words: "water pills" = a diuretic; "fell out" = fainted; "the fits" = seizures
slides.say: You met some interview techniques in Chapter 10; this chapter adds a few. Reflection means repeating the patient's own words, like can't breathe, so they keep talking without you leading them. Clarification means asking what they mean, and translating everyday words: my sugars means diabetes, water pills usually means a diuretic, fell out means fainted, and the fits means seizures. Empathy means showing you understand how they feel. Confrontation means calmly pointing out something that doesn't fit, like a story that doesn't match the scene; use it rarely, and never judge. Interpretation means saying what you think is going on, then checking. After each question, wait; a pause feels long to you, but not to them.
slides.sayZh: 第十章学过一些问诊技巧，本章再补几个。反映，就是重复病人自己的话，比如「喘不上气？」，让他接着说，而你不带诱导。澄清，就是问他是什么意思，并把日常说法翻译过来：my sugars 指糖尿病，water pills 通常指利尿剂，fell out 指晕倒，the fits 指癫痫发作。共情，是让病人感到你理解他的感受。对质，是平静地指出不吻合的地方，比如说法和现场对不上；尽量少用，绝不评判。解释，是说出你认为发生了什么，再向病人核实。每问一句都要等；你觉得停顿很长，对方并不觉得。

slides.title: OPQRST, and BC's versions
slides.body:
LetterAsk
OnsetWhen did it start?
ProvocationWhat brought it on? Sudden? Better or worse with…?
QualityWhat does it feel like, in your words?
Region, radiation, referralPoint with one finger. Does it travel?
Severity1 to 10, 10 = the worst ever
TimeHow long has it lasted?
  • BC scoring manual: OPQRRRST and LOTARP
slides.say: The book uses OPQRST to unpack a complaint like pain. Onset: when did it start? Provocation: what brought it on, did it come suddenly or slowly, and what makes it better or worse? Quality: what does it feel like, in the patient's own words? Region, radiation and referral: point to it with one finger; does it stay there or travel? Severity: on a scale of one to ten, where ten is the worst pain ever. Time: how long has it lasted? Write down the score, and how distressed the patient looks. For the BC exam, note that the BC scoring manual uses two mnemonics, OPQRRRST and LOTARP. Learn the exact letters from your program's copy of the manual.
slides.sayZh: 书里用 OPQRST 来拆解像疼痛这样的主诉。O 起病：什么时候开始的？P 诱因：什么引起的？突然还是慢慢来的？什么让它好转或加重？Q 性质：用病人自己的话说是什么感觉？R 部位、放射、牵涉：用一根手指指出来，是固定在那儿还是会跑？S 严重度：一到十分，十分是这辈子最痛。T 时间：持续多久了？把评分写下来，也记下病人看上去有多痛苦。考 BC 要注意：BC 评分手册用两个口诀，OPQRRRST 和 LOTARP，具体字母以你课程发的评分手册为准。

slides.title: The functional enquiry: PCP only
slides.body:
BC secondary survey = history, vital signs, head-to-toe exam, and a functional inquiry (PCP required). EMRs don't do it.

The 9 systems in the BC practical grading criteria:

General healthCentral nervous systemRespiratory
CardiovascularGI / GUIntegumentary (skin)
MusculoskeletalEndocrineEENT
slides.say: Here's the biggest new piece of history-taking for you. In the BC assessment model, the secondary survey includes the history, the vital signs, a head-to-toe exam, and a functional inquiry, which is required for PCPs. EMRs don't do it. A functional enquiry is a short, organised walk through the body systems, so problems the patient didn't mention don't slip past you. The BC practical grading criteria list nine systems: general health, the central nervous system, respiratory, cardiovascular, GI and GU, meaning the gut and the urinary and genital organs, integumentary, meaning the skin, musculoskeletal, endocrine, and EENT, the eyes, ears, nose and throat. The textbook hints at the same habit: finish the history with a quick check of the body systems.
slides.sayZh: 这是病史采集里对你来说最大的新内容。BC 评估模型的二次评估包括病史、生命体征、从头到脚的体检，以及系统问诊，而系统问诊是 PCP 必做的，EMR 不做。系统问诊就是按身体系统有条理地快速过一遍，免得病人没提到的问题从你眼皮底下溜走。BC 实操评分标准列了九个系统：一般健康、中枢神经系统、呼吸、心血管、GI/GU（即消化道和泌尿生殖系统）、皮肤（integumentary）、肌肉骨骼、内分泌，以及 EENT（眼、耳、鼻、喉）。课本也提到同样的习惯：病史最后快速查一遍各个身体系统。

slides.title: For the BC exam: how it's marked
slides.body:
−5%system not askedper system
−3%asked, but missed info pertinent to the chief complaintper system
−1%missed info not pertinentper system
  • Whole functional enquiry: maximum 15% deducted
  • No deduction if history is unavailable or the patient is unresponsive
  • Grading criteria: "Functional Enquiries – PCP ONLY"
slides.say: Here's how the EMALB practical grading criteria mark it, system by system. If you don't ask about a system at all, you lose five percent. If you ask, but miss information that is pertinent to the chief complaint, you lose three percent. If you miss information that isn't pertinent, you lose one percent. The whole functional enquiry is capped at fifteen percent, but remember that a scenario score under seventy percent means you're assigned another scenario, so every point counts. There's no deduction when the history is unavailable or the patient is unresponsive. The practical lesson: touch all nine systems every time, briefly, and dig deeper in the systems linked to the chief complaint.
slides.sayZh: EMALB 实操评分标准是按系统逐个扣分的。某个系统完全没问，扣百分之五；问了，但漏掉与主诉相关的信息，扣百分之三；漏掉与主诉无关的信息，扣百分之一。整个系统问诊最多扣百分之十五；但别忘了，一个场景得分低于百分之七十就要再考一个场景，所以每一分都重要。病史无法获得或病人无反应时不扣分。实际做法是：每次九个系统都要快速过一遍，和主诉有关的系统要问得更深。

slides.q: In your PCP practical, an alert patient complains of abdominal pain. You ask about every system except GI/GU. What is the deduction for that system?
options: None: the functional enquiry is optional
slides.say: Here's a BC exam question. In your PCP practical, an alert patient complains of abdominal pain. You go through every system except GI and GU. What's the deduction for that system? A, none, because the functional enquiry is optional. B, one percent. C, three percent. D, five percent. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 BC 考试题。PCP 实操考试中，一位清醒的病人主诉腹痛。你问遍了所有系统，唯独漏了 GI/GU。这个系统扣多少？A 不扣，系统问诊是选做；B 百分之一；C 百分之三；D 百分之五。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is D, five percent. A system that isn't asked at all costs five percent. Three percent is for asking but missing information pertinent to the chief complaint, and one percent is for missing information that isn't pertinent. A is wrong: the functional enquiry is required for PCPs, and the only exceptions are an unavailable history or an unresponsive patient, and this patient is alert. Skipping the GI system in abdominal pain also means losing your most important clues.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 D，百分之五。一个系统完全没问扣百分之五；问了但漏掉与主诉相关的信息扣百分之三；漏掉无关信息扣百分之一。A 错：系统问诊是 PCP 必做的，只有病史无法获得或病人无反应时例外，而这位病人是清醒的。腹痛却漏问消化系统，也等于丢掉了最重要的线索。

slides.title: Hard histories
slides.body:
• Major trauma, alcohol, "no neck pain"? Still restrict spinal motion
  • Suspected abuse: separate the partner, ask alone; police if needed
  • Hints of suicide: ask directly about thoughts and a plan
  • Anxiety that won't settle: early shock? hypoxia? something hidden?
  • Altered mental status: check glucose, diabetic or not
  • Language barrier: a trained interpreter, not a child, if possible
slides.say: Some histories are hard to get. Alcohol and drugs make the history unreliable and can hide pain, so after major trauma, an intoxicated patient who denies neck pain still needs spinal motion restriction. If you suspect abuse, don't accuse anyone on scene; find a reason to separate the partner, ask the patient alone, and call police when needed. If a patient hints at suicide, ask directly whether they're thinking of it and whether they have a plan. Anxiety should settle once you arrive; if it doesn't, think of early shock, hypoxia, or something the patient is hiding. Check the blood glucose in anyone with altered mental status, even without a diabetes history. And use a proper interpreter when you can.
slides.sayZh: 有些病史很难拿到。酒精和药物会让病史不可靠，还会掩盖疼痛，所以重大创伤后，一个喝醉、说脖子不痛的病人仍然需要限制脊柱活动。怀疑家暴时不要在现场指控任何人；找个理由支开伴侣，单独问病人，需要时叫警察。病人流露轻生念头时，要直接问他是否想自杀、有没有计划。你到场后焦虑本应平复；如果没有，要想到早期休克、缺氧，或病人在隐瞒什么。意识改变的人都要测血糖，哪怕没有糖尿病史。语言不通时，尽量找正规口译。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: what your history decides
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Obtain a history and a baseline set of vital signs
  • Chest pain: history includes a pain assessment
  • Overdose, diabetic: vitals include blood glucose
  • EMR drugs: ASA already taken? Erectile drug before nitro?

PCP adds

  • Functional inquiry: 9 systems, required
  • TXA: time of injury (not over 3 h), age, isolated head injury?
  • Ondansetron: long QT? early pregnancy?
  • Dexamethasone: fungal infection? steroid allergy?
  • IV fluids: evidence of real blood or fluid loss
slides.say: On the left is what every licence level does. Many BC protocols say: obtain a history and a baseline set of vital signs. For chest pain, the history includes a pain assessment; for an overdose or a diabetic emergency, the vital signs include a blood glucose. You already check history before your EMR drugs, like whether the patient took aspirin already, or used an erectile dysfunction drug before nitroglycerin. On the right is what the PCP adds: the required functional inquiry. Then the history behind your new drugs: for TXA, the time of injury, the age, and whether it's an isolated head injury; for ondansetron, long QT and early pregnancy; for dexamethasone, a fungal infection or a steroid allergy. And for IV fluids, BC wants evidence of real blood or fluid loss.
slides.sayZh: 左栏是所有执照级别都做的：很多 BC 流程都写着——采集病史和一组基线生命体征。胸痛的病史要包括疼痛评估；过量用药或糖尿病急症的生命体征要包括血糖。你给 EMR 药之前本来就要问病史，比如病人是否已经吃过阿司匹林、用硝酸甘油前是否用过治疗勃起功能障碍的药。右栏是 PCP 多出来的：必做的系统问诊。然后是新药背后的病史：TXA 要问受伤时间、年龄、是否单纯颅脑外伤；昂丹司琼要问长 QT 和早期妊娠；地塞米松要问全身真菌感染和激素过敏。补液方面，BC 要求有确实失血或失液的证据。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Every PCP drug has history-based stops: ask before you give
  • Don't anchor on dispatch, a chart label or the patient's self-diagnosis
  • Unreliable source (alcohol, confusion)? A "no" rules nothing out
  • Document who told you what, and the pain score
  • Critical patient: life threats first; keep the history short
  • Functional enquiry: brief, complete, every time
slides.say: So what's new to watch out for? Every PCP drug has stops that only the history can reveal, so ask before you give, not after. Don't anchor on the dispatch note, a label in the chart, or the patient's own diagnosis. When the source is unreliable, because of alcohol, drugs or confusion, a simple no can't rule out a serious injury. Document where each piece of information came from, and record the pain score. For a critical patient, fix the life threats first; the book notes you may have no time for the long list of health questions. And make the functional enquiry a habit: brief, but complete, every time.
slides.sayZh: 那么有哪些新的注意事项？每种 PCP 药都有只有病史才能发现的禁忌，所以要先问后给，而不是给了再问。不要被派单备注、病历上的标签或病人自己的诊断锚住。信息来源不可靠时，比如酒精、药物或意识混乱，一句「没有」排除不了严重损伤。记录每条信息是谁说的，也记下疼痛评分。危重病人先处理生命威胁；书里也说，这时你可能没时间问那一长串健康问题。系统问诊要养成习惯：简短，但完整，每次都做。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Turn every complaint into 4–5 possibilities; rule out the worst first
  2. Organised history: OPQRST in the book; OPQRRRST and LOTARP for BC
  3. PCP only: the functional enquiry (9 systems) and history checks before every new drug

Next: Chapter 16, Physical Examination
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: turn every chief complaint into four or five possibilities, and rule out the worst first, even for a patient you've seen many times. Two: take an organised history. The book uses OPQRST; for BC, know OPQRRRST and LOTARP. Three: two things are yours alone as a PCP: the functional enquiry, nine systems, required in the BC secondary survey, and the history checks before every new PCP drug. Next class, we move from asking to examining, in Chapter 16, the physical examination. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，把每个主诉展开成四到五个可能，先排除最坏的，哪怕是见过很多次的病人。二，病史要有条理：书里用 OPQRST，考 BC 要会 OPQRRRST 和 LOTARP。三，有两件事只属于 PCP：系统问诊——九个系统，BC 二次评估必做；以及每种 PCP 新药给药前的病史核查。下节课从「问」转到「查」，第十六章体格检查。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
